scope: First sourced Georgian blog article; research of search intent and competing result pages, not a complete ranking or search-volume audit.
decision: Support the existing daily-pay listing with an informational guide about rates, hours and payment dates. Keep the listing as the destination for people seeking current jobs.

siteEvidence.limitation: Historical, small sample. These are JOBX impressions and clicks, not total search demand. No fresh GSC data or keyword-volume estimates were obtained during this research.

competingPages.observation: Archived listing distinguished a daily rate from twice-monthly payments during research. It is not mentioned, linked or used as a real example in the current public article.
Recruitment page targets laborer and driver roles with daily rates and direct contact. It serves vacancy/application intent. No inference about ranking position or general market wages.

Expired vacancy displays a monthly label in the header but a daily rate in the body. This illustrates why readers should check the full conditions. Not used to generalize about that site's reliability or copied into the article.

primarySources.use: Essential employment terms, overtime agreement and payment frequency; latest consolidated HTML checked.
Historical research only. Removed from the public article at the user's request.
Editorial approach only: original useful comparison and source attribution. Not a source for employment or legal claims.

implementation.primaryIntent: Understand and compare daily pay before accepting work
implementation.originalValue: Explicitly illustrative hourly comparison, monthly-day arithmetic and five practical employer questions
implementation.sources: Research records remain in this document. At the user's request, public articles no longer display source lists, inline citation links, review labels or source URLs in structured data.
implementation.seo: Unique title, description, self-canonical, visible headings, BlogPosting and breadcrumbs, static HTML, sitemap, contextual links in both directions
implementation.publication: Published on JOBX. The competitor listing example was subsequently removed and replaced by an explicitly hypothetical payment-schedule example; no actual job or market rate is claimed.
implementation.measurementAfterRelease: Compare non-brand blog and daily-pay landing impressions/clicks in equivalent GSC periods. Assess queries and landing-page overlap. No ranking or traffic gain is promised.
